method: Dimension-specific piecewise annual estimates using official structural history plus existing FIFA Big Count 2006 and FIFA Professional Football Report 2023 observations with strict temporal gating.
evidence_rules: A 9.0+ score means world-leading for that dimension; it is not awarded merely because a federation, centre or programme exists.
Confidence describes the authored rating estimate, not confidence that the cited official fact exists.
Big Count 2006 anchors popularity/access only and retains its mixed-sex and cross-country-definition limitations.
Professional 2023 player/club counts inform competition and elite-ecosystem depth; they do not directly measure development quality.
France's DTN, INF and Clairefontaine milestones are development/elite-support evidence from their dated years only.
Spain's Ciudad del Fútbol is elite/development capacity evidence, not nationwide public access evidence.
The 2026 RFEF talent process is programme-capacity evidence and is not treated as a measured development outcome.
No held-out validation ranking is used for score tuning.

country_notes.FRA: Deep pre-1955 institutional/professional continuity, strong 2006 participation footprint and unusually rich long-run technical-development evidence support high modern ratings, while direct popularity/access data remains sparse after 2006.
country_notes.ESP: Long federation continuity, large 2006 participation footprint, a deep 2023 professional ecosystem and modern national training/talent infrastructure support a strong modern profile; historical development and competition estimates remain lower confidence where direct period evidence is sparse.
